unit.why: A homiletic exhortation (night prayer, Psalms, supporting true scholars and tsaddikim) built around one embedded narrative: R. Zusha of Anipoli's three-day fasts and the miraculous milk and honey nursing that sustained him, told through a chain of transmission.
unit.boundary_note: the story is embedded in a sermon frame that runs before and after it; the division ends with the heading of the next section ('מענין מצוה לשמוע דברי חכמים')

stories.start_quote: וסיפר לי מו״ח הצדיק המפורסם מוהר״ר
stories.summary_en: R. Zusha, a poor beadle in Ostroh who fasted for days, decided that begging for bread showed a lack of faith; when no one was worthy to feed him, God made him two nipples in his mouth giving honey and milk, which fed him for three months until a man handed him coins for bread.

quotes: והיה דרכו להתענות שנים ושלשה ימים
tags.why: his habitual multi-day fasts drive the plot

quotes: והתענה והלך עד שהיה קרוב למות
tags.why: extreme self-denial, fasting nearly to death

quotes: שני דדין בפיו אחד הוציא דבש
אזי ברגע נפסק זה הדבש וחלב
tags.why: a discrete miracle of miraculous nourishment

quotes: שזהו חסרון אמונה לילך ולבקש לחם
tags.why: he chooses not to beg, accepting poverty out of trust in God
the story illustrates Zusha's faith and trust in God

quotes: יבטח באלהיו באמונה שלימה שלא יחסר מזונו
tags.why: faith and trust are the virtue at issue

quotes: שיתן לו על לחם להשיב נפשו
זוסא קח לך ששה גראשיש וקנה לך לחם
tags.why: giving to the poor tsaddik, and the merit of doing so, is the point of the story and its frame

quotes: ששמע מאיש וכו׳ קדוש מוהר״ר זוסא
tags.why: the text frames the tale as told by the tsaddik himself and handed on
the narrative is wrapped in an extended homiletic exhortation

quotes: שתתקשר לצדיק אמת כי על ידי התקשרות
tags.why: the frame urges attachment to and support of a true tsaddik

missing_concepts: trust in God (bitachon) versus asking for sustenance
the worthiness or merit needed to perform a mitzvah (supporting a true scholar)
